legend.fallback: No finer data; keeping the {level} level.
legend.ec02: Real data: SII F2890, deeds {from}–{to}. All property types, no floor area.
legend.in04: Real data: DTPM GTFS, weekday 7–9 am, stops within 500 m straight line. Zones without buildings shown faint.
legend.in01: Real data: Overture Maps and DTPM GTFS. Grocery, pharmacy, primary care and transit; 100 = all within 5 min, 0 = 20+ min. Minutes estimated from straight-line distance.
legend.so01: Real data: INE Census 2024 by block. Residents per km² of each cell; for the comuna, the density the average resident lives at (empty hills don't dilute it).
legend.en03: Real data: Greater Santiago Urban Noise Map 2023 (MMA, 2024). Mean daytime Ld in the open space of blocks, excluding carriageways; 5 dB classes.
legend.hazards: Real data: MINVU RM (PRMS risk areas and hazard studies). % of residents (Census 2024) living inside the official zone. Each hazard separately; outside a polygon does not mean no risk.
legend.en04: Real data: Sentinel-2 (Copernicus), 17 January 2026, 10 m. Mean NDVI: in the dry summer only trees and irrigation stay green.
legend.climate: Real data: ARClim (MMA, CR2), historical climate 1980–2010 by comuna (~5 km model, no neighbourhood detail).
legend.rs03: Real data: INE and SPD, ENUSC 2024 small-area estimates (experimental statistics). % of households victim of a violent crime in 12 months; comuna level only.
legend.en01: Real data: SINCA (MMA), 10 stations in the Metropolitan Region, annual mean 2023–2025. Comuna value interpolated from stations: a coarse surface.
legend.rs01: Real data: CEAD, Ministry of Public Security, 2025 police cases. Crimes against life or physical integrity + violent robberies per 100k residents; counted where they happen, so commercial comunas rank high.
legend.composite: 0–100 index of how a place compares with the rest of Greater Santiago: the average of climate, environment, daily life and safety & risks. No prices or density. A first impression; each layer has the detail.

drawer.label: Selected place card
drawer.demoNote: Sale prices, transit and daily services are real data; other values in this build are synthetic. Comuna geometries are real.
drawer.teaserTitle: The information. And what it means.
drawer.teaserText: Estimated value, records, surroundings and priority checks in a single report.
drawer.method_EC02: SII form F2890 (registered transfers). Sales from 500 to 100,000 UF; a deal covering several rols (apartment + parking + storage) counts once. No type or floor area until the SII catastro is joined.
drawer.method_EC01: SII: catastro (Detalle Catastral 2026-2) + F2890 sales of the last 24 months. Deals with a single homes rol; price in UF divided by that rol's built m² (parking and storage included in the price). Median per comuna.
drawer.method_IN04: DTPM GTFS (Red Metropolitana de Movilidad). Weekday 7–9 am departures per hour at stops and stations within 500 m straight line of the zone center; not walking time over streets. Comuna: zone average weighted by building count (Overture).
drawer.accNote: Estimated minutes: straight line ×1.3 at 4.5 km/h, not an actual route.
drawer.method_IN01: Overture Maps (places with confidence ≥0.5) and DTPM GTFS stops. Four equally weighted groups: grocery, pharmacy, primary care, transit; score 100 at ≤5 min, 0 at ≥20 min. Minutes estimated from straight-line distance ×1.3 at 4.5 km/h. Measures distance, not service quality.
drawer.method_SO01: INE Census 2024 block cartography (n_per). Each block is assigned to the ~600 m cell containing its center; gross density = residents / cell area. Comuna value: population-weighted mean of cell densities. Cells without residents have no value.
drawer.method_EN03: MMA Greater Santiago Urban Noise Map 2023 (published April 2024). The day map (Ld) is published as colored tiles; we decode each ~30 m pixel to its 5 dB class and average pixels below 75 dBA within the cell (carriageways are drawn above 75, buildings have no value). Comuna: population-weighted mean (Census 2024). Official exposure by comuna (residents above 65 dBA day, 55 dBA night) is shown in the card.
drawer.noiseExposure: Official MMA: {day}% of residents above 65 dBA by day, {night}% above 55 dBA at night.
drawer.method_RS07: MINVU SEREMI/SERVIU RM, OTRAS_AMENAZAS_RMS service. Flooding: PRMS recurrently floodable areas and groundwater outcrop, high flood zone, river floods and hyperconcentrated flows. Mass movement: PRMS landslide and collapse areas, high-hazard debris flows. Seismic: soils with very poor seismic response. Value: % of Census 2024 residents (block centers) inside the area; hazards are not summed. Metropolitan source scale: not a substitute for a site study.
drawer.method_RS09: MINVU SEREMI/SERVIU RM, OTRAS_AMENAZAS_RMS service. Flooding: PRMS recurrently floodable areas and groundwater outcrop, high flood zone, river floods and hyperconcentrated flows. Mass movement: PRMS landslide and collapse areas, high-hazard debris flows. Seismic: soils with very poor seismic response. Value: % of Census 2024 residents (block centers) inside the area; hazards are not summed. Metropolitan source scale: not a substitute for a site study.
drawer.method_RS05: MINVU SEREMI/SERVIU RM, OTRAS_AMENAZAS_RMS service. Flooding: PRMS recurrently floodable areas and groundwater outcrop, high flood zone, river floods and hyperconcentrated flows. Mass movement: PRMS landslide and collapse areas, high-hazard debris flows. Seismic: soils with very poor seismic response. Value: % of Census 2024 residents (block centers) inside the area; hazards are not summed. Metropolitan source scale: not a substitute for a site study.
drawer.faultKm: Distance to the San Ramón fault (MINVU trace): {km} km.
drawer.method_EN04: Sentinel-2 L2A (Copernicus, ESA), cloud-free scene of 2026-01-17, tiles 19HCD and 19HCC via Element84 COGs on AWS. NDVI = (B8 − B4)/(B8 + B4) at 10 m; clouds, shadows and water removed using the SCL band. Cell: mean of its pixels. Comuna: Census 2024 population-weighted mean. One summer date: measures green cover, not park quality.
drawer.method_CL01: ARClim (Ministry of Environment, CR2), comunas layer: days per year with maximum above 30 °C, historical period 1980–2010. The card shows the projected change to 2035–2065 under SSP2-4.5 (model mean). Source resolution ~5 km: comuna level only.
drawer.method_CL03: ARClim (MMA, CR2), comunas layer: annual accumulated precipitation, historical period 1980–2010. The card shows the projected change to 2035–2065 under SSP2-4.5. The post-2010 megadrought is not in the historical mean.
drawer.method_RS03: INE and Undersecretariat for Crime Prevention: comuna SAE estimates of the ENUSC 2024 VHDV indicator (experimental statistics) with 95% confidence interval. Measures households victim of robbery with violence or intimidation, snatching and assault. Not downscaled to neighbourhoods.
drawer.method_EN01: SINCA (Ministry of Environment): daily validated (or preliminary) PM2.5 from 10 Metropolitan Region stations, 2023–2025; years with ≥75% of days. Comuna value: inverse-distance-squared interpolation to the comuna's population centre. With few stations this is coarse; the card shows the nearest station. Chilean annual standard: 20 µg/m³.
drawer.airStation: Nearest station: {st}, {v} µg/m³ measured, {km} km away.
drawer.method_RS01: CEAD (Ministry of Public Security): 2025 police cases (reports + in-flagrante arrests) in the families 'crimes against life or physical integrity' and 'violent robberies'; annual rate per 100k residents = sum of monthly rates. Counted where the crime happened, not where the victim lives: comunas with a large daytime population (Santiago, Providencia) get inflated per-resident rates. Comuna level only.
drawer.crimeChange: Change vs 2024: {chg}%. Non-violent property crime: {prop} per 100k.
drawer.method_QX00: Average over families (climate, environment, daily life, safety & risks) of the percentiles of their real layers, oriented so that 100 is best. Prices, density and rain are left out.
drawer.reportHint: Evaluating a property? Zoom in and tap a building: you get its free card and can order the full report.

about.title: Everything about a place and a property, on one map.
about.lead: PROMETEO is a real-estate atlas of Chile. It brings together official data on environment, infrastructure, safety and actual sale prices so anyone can understand what is going on in a place and what it is worth. We start with Santiago and the Metropolitan Region.
about.problemText: Understanding a single address today means collecting data from more than ten institutions (SII, CEAD, MMA, MINVU, INE, DTPM), each with its own format and scale. Portals show asking prices, not sale prices, and neighbourhoods are judged by opinions. PROMETEO turns days of work into a one-minute query.

stats.s2: SII cadastre roles: use, floor area, year, assessed value

about.how1Text: An address, an SII rol or a phrase like “quiet, green and near the metro”.
about.how2Text: City, comuna, ~600 m zone, block and building. Each scale shows its own layers; broader ones stay in the background.
about.how3Text: The building card is free. The full PDF report assesses value, strengths and risks against sales of the same property type.
about.layersLead: Six layer families and an overall 0–100 place quality index.
about.f3Text: Shops, health, schools and transit on foot (GTFS). Coming soon: mobile coverage and internet speed.
about.f6Text: UF/m² from actual sales, trends and sales volume.
about.m1: Every number keeps its source, date, scale and coverage.
about.m2: 0–100 indices with fixed weights per topic group: five corner shops do not outweigh a health centre.
about.m3: Natural hazards are not offset by nearby cafés; price is not mistaken for quality; social data never becomes a ranking of people.
about.m4: “No data” does not mean “bad”: gaps are shown as gaps.
about.m5: In the report, code computes every figure and chart; AI only writes the conclusions. Numbers are not made up.
about.m6: Only official and open data, and only aggregates on the map: no personal data.
about.for1Text: Understand the neighbourhood and a fair price before making an offer.
about.for2Text: Compare comunas and zones, spot undervalued areas and prepare reports for clients.
about.for3Text: Access to services, infrastructure gaps, noise, heat, connectivity and data coverage.
about.r1Text: Santiago and the Metropolitan Region: layers, cadastre, valuation by unit type, reports and trends.
about.r2Text: All of Chile, a mobile and internet coverage layer, building photos.
about.r3Text: Widget and index for portals, API and dashboards for institutions.
about.r4Text: All of Latin America, and then the world.
about.unitTitle: New: the value of your unit, not the neighbourhood average
about.unitLead: PROMETEO reads the composition of every building in the SII cadastre and values the specific unit you pick against actual sales of the same type.
about.u1: Building composition: for example, 89 offices, 6 shops, 717 parking spaces and 35 storage units.
about.u2: Pick your unit (DP 501, OF 32) in the card or when buying the report.
about.u3: Compared only with sales of the same type: apartments, houses, offices, shops, industrial and land; parking and storage per unit.
about.u4: The benchmark comes from the most precise level with enough sales: ~1 km zone, then comuna, then region.
about.u5: The report gives a value range for the unit with the median UF/m² and the number of sales, and the AI writes the conclusions and the checklist for that property type.
about.uStats: Based on 67k apartment sales, 35k house sales and 49k parking and storage sales (SII F2890, 10/2024–09/2026), plus offices, shops, industrial and land.

trends.lead: Compare the {n} comunas of Greater Santiago across every layer with real data and see how they change over time.
trends.rankSub: pick the layer with the buttons; click a bar to pick that comuna
trends.profileSub: Where the comuna stands among Santiago's comunas on each layer (left = lowest value). Colour says whether that is favourable.
trends.crimeSub: % change in the rate per 100k residents (CEAD). Red = up, blue = down.
trends.heatSub: Days per year above 30 °C, historical 1980–2010 and projected 2035–2065 SSP2-4.5 (ARClim)
trends.scatterSub: Each dot is a comuna. The dashed line is the trend; r measures how closely the two layers move together (−1 to 1).
trends.foot: Open data processed by PROMETEO. Each layer's method is in the map (Sources and coverage). Comuna-level values; zone layers are aggregated weighted by population.
trends.lockText: Every layer and comuna, prices over time, crime, climate, layer relationships and data download.
trends.pickCompare: Pick up to {max} comunas to compare
trends.compareHint: Add another comuna to compare them side by side.
trends.cmpSub: 0–100 score against the other comunas (50 = middle of Santiago, higher is better). Same method as the map's overall index.
trends.tableSub: Bold = best value of the group where the layer has a clear direction (more services, less noise…). Prices and density are not rated.
trends.tableNote: #n = rank among the {n} comunas (1 = highest value).
trends.priceSub_median: Yearly median sale price in UF (SII F2890), all property types. Dashed line: median of the comunas.
trends.priceSub_index: Yearly median as an index (first year = 100): shows who rose most, whatever the price level.
trends.priceSub_deals: Registered sales per year: how much the market moves (liquidity).
trends.chgSub: Change of the yearly median sale price, {from} → {to}, in %
trends.chgNote: All property types mixed: a shift in what is being sold (more new flats, for example) also moves the median.
trends.rangeSub: The middle half of sales (25th–75th percentile) and the median, in UF, last 24 months. A long bar = a very mixed market.
trends.turnSub: Sales in {year} per 1,000 residents (SII F2890, Census 2024). Higher = easier to buy and sell.
trends.r_neg: one rises as the other falls
trends.presetNote_value: Do people pay more where life is better? Comunas below the line cost less per m² than their overall index suggests.
trends.presetNote_services: How much people pay for daily services within walking distance.
trends.presetNote_green: Greener comunas tend to be quieter; the ones off the trend are the exceptions.
trends.presetNote_transit: Whether transit supply keeps up with population density.
trends.valueNote: Distance from the trend line. A simple comparison between comunas, not a valuation.
trends.chgSub_: Change of the yearly median sale price, in %

reportInfo.title: The full property report
reportInfo.lead: A 4-page analysis of one specific address, ready in a minute and downloadable as a PDF. It puts in one document what usually takes days: official data from more than ten open sources crossed for that point, and a clear reading of what it means for buying, selling or investing.

pricing.title: Decide with data, not gut feeling
pricing.lead: Each report gathers in a minute what takes days to collect: real SII sale prices, official hazards, surroundings, transit and what to check before you sign. Choose by how many properties you analyse.
pricing.plansSub: For people who analyse properties every month. They include full Data and trends and the best price per report.
pricing.planFor_basic: Active buyers and investors who look at a few properties a month.
pricing.planFor_partner: Agents and teams who back every listing and recommendation with data.
pricing.planFor_unlimited: Developers, flippers and offices with a steady flow of properties.
pricing.planSave: {each} per report; {n} single reports would cost {value}
pricing.unlimitedSave: Unlimited reports: pays off from {n} reports a month
pricing.fTrends: Full Data and trends: all comunas on every layer
pricing.fCompare: Prices over time and comuna comparison
pricing.plansNote: Monthly, in Chilean pesos. Cancel any time from your account; the plan stays active until the end of the paid period. Plan reports renew every month and do not roll over.
pricing.packsSub: For one-off work, no subscription. Reports stay in your account and you use them whenever you like.
pricing.plansBetter: Why a plan rather than a pack? Besides reports it includes full Data and trends: rankings of every comuna, prices year by year, comparison and data download, which packs do not include.
pricing.singleText: No sign-up: pick the building on the map, pay by card and the report opens right away.
pricing.why1: A home in Santiago is decided in thousands of UF. A location mistake, such as a flood zone, night-time noise, a comuna whose prices stall or a metro further away than the listing says, costs far more than the report, and almost never appears in the listing.
pricing.why2: PROMETEO crosses official data from SII, MINVU, INE, MMA, DTPM and other sources for every address and turns it into a verdict, risks with their evidence, the real comuna price and a list of what to check before you sign. What takes a professional an afternoon of searching is here in a minute.
pricing.why3: Agents use it to back a recommendation and win the client's trust; investors and flippers to rule out fast and negotiate with arguments; buyers to avoid overpaying and surprises. One well-supported negotiation argument can be worth more than the report.
pricing.a_account: Not for a single report: you pay and it opens. Packs and plans belong to the e-mail you pay with; you sign in with a link sent to that e-mail, no password.
pricing.a_cancel: Yes, any time, from your account (Billing and cancellation). No commitment; the plan stays active until the end of the paid month.
pricing.q_unused: What happens to plan reports I do not use?
pricing.a_unused: They renew every month and do not roll over. If you need more, add a pack or change plan.
pricing.a_single: A 4-page PDF report on the chosen address: verdict, scores, strengths and risks with evidence, comuna price and trend, official hazards, walking times, who it suits, what to check and negotiation arguments. See the sample with the "?" button.
pricing.a_pay: By credit or debit card through Stripe, in Chilean pesos. PROMETEO never sees or stores your card details.
pricing.q_data: Where does the data come from?
pricing.a_data: Official and open sources: SII, INE, MINVU, MMA, DTPM, CEAD, ARClim, satellite imagery and OpenStreetMap. Each layer's method is in "Sources and coverage".
pricing.legal: Reports are indicative: they are not a valuation or legal or financial advice.
